messages:
sophie: Heads-up — ACME APAC complaining about p95/p99 latency and intermittent 500s for embed calls since ~03:05 UTC. Started right after last infra rollout. Customer reports tail latency ~4-6s (normal ~200ms). Repro steps they sent below.

sophie: repro steps: curl to https://api.apac.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":"<batch of 8 long docs>"}' -> 500 or 4s+. Happens across multiple API keys for them.

olivia: oncall here. Thanks — looking. Can you paste the trace id from the 500s? Also which nodes are serving APAC traffic?

sophie: trace ids: tx=apac:0a1b2c3d, apac:0a1b2c99. Frontend logs show repeated upstream timeouts to runtime pool. Affected nodes: apac-run-03, apac-run-07, apac-run-12 (per routing logs).

infra-bot: [alert] Region=apac metric=api.p99 latency spike from 180ms -> 4100ms; error.rate 5% -> 28% over last 6m. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-174912

oncall: grabbing iostat and dmesg from apac-run-07. Sharing quick snippets.

oncall: `iostat -x 1 3` -> apac-nvme0 avg await=12.9ms -> spiking to 350ms in bursts. cpu iowait up to 40%.

oncall: `dmesg | tail -n 40` -> repeated: "nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting" and some firmware messages.

raj: interesting — we recently rolled CUDA/runtime driver package 15.0.2 to APAC fleet last night. Kernel + nvme/pci power management interactions can cause tail IO spikes with certain firmware combos. Could be NVMe queue depth or driver interaction.

olivia: can we confirm kernel version and nvme firmware on the affected hosts?

oncall: apac-run-07: kernel 6.5.4, nvme fw 2.3.1, gpu driver 515 -> was upgraded to 520 ~2024-06-08, bundle shows cuda15 packages. apac-run-03 same.

raj: hmm — similar pattern to earlier host-io regressions: driver change + kernel preemption + NVMe queue depth causing long io stalls under heavy KV cache churn. Two immediate mitigations: 1) divert APAC traffic to eu fallback until we triage, 2) cordon + drain 1-2 canary nodes and roll back driver there to confirm.

olivia: starting traffic diversion: switching route policy to fallback-region for embeddings. Will keep low-risk hosted traffic in APAC for other routes. 

support-bot: Noted. Customer ACME notified: "We see elevated latency. We're investigating and routing to fallback region to reduce impact. Will update in 30m." :thumbsup:

oncall: cordoning apac-run-07 and draining. `kubectl cordon apac-run-07 && kubectl drain apac-run-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m`

oncall: deployed rollback job on canary apac-run-12 to revert gpu driver from 520 -> 515 and reinstalled nvme firmware compat package (dry-run). Command used: ```bash
ssh infra@apac-run-12 'sudo apt-get install --allow-downgrades nvidia-driver-515 -y && sudo reboot'
```

raj: good. While that boots, can someone run a quick synthetic load to reproduce p99 on an unaffected node (apac-run-02) and compare iostat/dmesg? Use the internal loadgen: `./tools/loadgen --region apac --model embed-large --batch 8 --rps 40 --duration 300`

olivia: running loadgen now on apac-run-02. Early results: p99 ~220ms -> stable. On apac-run-07 pre-cordon, loadgen shows p99 spikes 2.1s correlating with nvme timeouts in dmesg.

raj: that strongly points to host-level storage IO stalls on a subset of nodes (likely firmware driver coupling). Plan: 1) maintain traffic diversion to fallback, 2) finish rollback on canary and run regression test, 3) if canary stable, schedule staged rollback across affected pool, 4) open vendor escalation (nvme/gpu driver vendor) if rollback doesn't help.

sophie: assigned owners: olivia (mitigation + routing), raj (rollback plan + vendor comms), oncall (triage + logs), I'll keep customer updated. Created INC-174912 in PagerDuty and linked runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/host-io-tail.

olivia: estimate 20–45m to validate canary after reboot. Will post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

infra-bot: metric update: after partial diversion, error.rate down to 3%, apac p99 down to ~450ms (from 4s). Continuing monitoring.

sophie: thanks team. If rollback doesn't fix, fallback plan B: lift autoscale headroom for APAC dedicated pools and temporarily reduce batch size to lower kv cache churn. I'll coordinate that with product to avoid cost surprises for ACME.

raj: noting potential follow-ups: add nvme firmware and kernel compatibility checks in our rollout gating; extend canary window for driver bundles to 6h in APAC; add synthetic KV-heavy job in preflight. Filing feature request: https://tracker.redwood.ai/issue/INFRA-2049

olivia: canary back online and tests running — will report pass/fail in ~10m.

sophie: update: customer ack'd routing change and appreciates prompt action. We'll keep thread updated and escalate to vendor if rollback doesn't reduce nvme errors. :white_check_mark:
